 News › Learning News › He left ₹1 crore salary at Samsung in South Korea to chase his IAS dream: How IIT Bombay graduate Ka… He left ₹1 crore salary at Samsung in South Korea to chase his IAS dream: How IIT Bombay graduate Kanishak Kataria cracked UPSC Civil Services 2018 with AIR 1 on his first attempt
 Jasleen Taneja Updated: Nov 12, 2026, 14:04 IST UPSC Topper Kanishak Kataria: Left a Rs 1 Crore Job in South Korea to Crack AIR 1 Where many people dream of a high-paying job abroad, Kanishak Kataria had one but chose to walk away from it. He joined the Civil Services because he wanted to work with people and help them, and he topped the exam.
 Here is his journey and the study habits that helped him score his way to the top.
 Kanishak Kataria, from Rajasthan, completed his B.Tech in Computer Science from IIT Bombay, and then got a job through campus placement. He went to South Korea to work as a software engineer at Samsung Electronics.
 His family has a civil services background. His father is an IAS officer in Rajasthan, and his uncle is also in the civil services. 
 He calls them both his role models.
 Why did he leave Rs 1 crore job?
 Kanishak wanted to experience life outside India, so he took a job in South Korea. After working there for a year, his package rose to nearly Rs 1 crore.
 But he felt something missing. He was earning well, but wanted to connect with people and get a chance to help them. This yearning pulled him back to India. He shared that jobs in India paid about one-third of his old package, but he went ahead anyway.
 How did the UPSC journey begin?
 He started preparing for UPSC exam in 2017 and appeared for the same in 2018. His father was his main inspiration, but noone pressured him to take the exam and supported his decisions.
 Because he came from an engineering background, he took coaching at the start. He also began reading newspapers daily and kept up with the news right from the beginning.
 Kanishak Kataria’s UPSC preparation strategy
 Area What he did 
 Study hours 13 to 14 hours a day during Mains preparation 
 Optional subject Mathematics, chosen after advice from seniors. The syllabus is long, so he gave it more time. He liked the subject and did not feel bored. 
 Current affairs Read newspapers daily for the previous two years, plus online magazines and news 
 CSAT Looked at a few previous years’ question papers about 10 days before the exam and practised through test series 
 Social media Stayed low-key. He turned off Facebook and Twitter, checked Instagram once a day and put his phone away two months before the exam. He did not keep a phone in his study room. 
 Study groups Joined WhatsApp groups with friends to discuss studies 
 Did he expect Rank 1?
 Kanishak shared that his paper went well, but he expected his rank in the top 100.
 He also says he never thought about the result while preparing. His approach was to prepare, take the exam and deal with the result when it arrived. He did not put pressure on himself.
 Kanishak believes in hard work and optimism. In his words, “either I win or I learn.” He says one should see things positively and never give up.
 After the announcement of UPSC Result
 After his result got released, he credited his parents, his sister and his girlfriend. Kanishak said the four people who helped him most deserved the credit, and that he would have thanked anyone else in that place. His parents taught him to credit those who help you, and he said he did not expect such a reaction.
 Kanishak now wishes to serve the country and meet people’s expectations.
 Here's what UPSC aspirants can learn from his story
 Build the news habit early. Read a newspaper daily for a long period, not just in the last few months.
 Choose a subject and spend time on it if the syllabus is long.
 Limit distractions. Keep the phone out of the study room as the exam nears.
 Focus on preparation, not the result. Less pressure helps stay consistent.
 Practise with test series and use previous years’ papers to understand the pattern.
